# Product

<!-- impeccable:product-schema 1 -->

## Platform

web

## Users

Primary audience: people who want to learn about the chapel and how to visit it — pilgrims, hikers, and local residents in and around Gudbrandsdalen, Norway, as well as anyone seeking a quiet, open place. Donors are a secondary audience. The site is maintained by the user (Andreas); the chapel project is owned by an organization created by the four friends.

## Product Purpose

The site's primary job is to inform people about the chapel — Capella Reginae Norvegiae, known locally as Mariaslæen — and how to visit it. Fundraising and donor recognition are secondary.

Fine. The `text-on-surface-variant/60` in footer copyright — #43474e at 60% opacity on #fbf9f4 → blended ~ #8a8d90 → contrast ~2.9:1 — fails WCAG for small text. The footer copyright "© 2026 Mathias and his companions." at text-xs (12px) with 60% opacity on surface-bright — low contrast. Real a11y/design issue.

The ourlady image row: `md:col-span-7` main image with hotspot, `md:col-span-5 md:mt-16` for the close-up portrait. The offset (mt-16) is a nice editorial stagger. Fine.

Minor.

But the hardcoded white hero button `bg-white text-primary` — on dark themes, primary is cyan/green — white button + dark text — fine.

Would be fixed with uniform aspect ratio + object-contain... but object-cover crops drawings (bad for technical drawings). Actually object-cover on a technical drawing crops content — bad. content.thinking:
Key confirmations:

1. **`--radius: 0.125rem`** — Tailwind v4's `rounded` (bare) utility uses `var(--radius)` with a default of 0.25rem (theme.css line 508: `--radius: 0.25rem`). The site overrides `--radius: 0.125rem` (2px). So any `rounded` class = 2px. But they also override `--radius-lg`, `--radius-xl`, `--radius-2xl` to tighter values. That's a coherent tighter-radius system — deliberate. However, the token `--radius-xs` is left at default 0.125rem — duplicate of their bare `--radius`. Fine, deliberate.

2. **Font tokens**: `font-headline`, `font-label`, `font-sketch` used consistently in pages. But the Layout header/footer/nav uses arbitrary `font-['Newsreader']`, `font-['Plus_Jakarta_Sans']`, `font-['Epilogue']` — the arbitrary value syntax `font-['Plus_Jakarta_Sans']` — underscores become spaces in Tailwind arbitrary values, good. But these bypass the token fallbacks (e.g., `font-['Newsreader']` produces `font-family: Newsreader` with no serif fallback? Actually Tailwind arbitrary `font-['Newsreader']` → `font-family: Newsreader;` — no fallback list). If the Google Fonts load fails or is blocked, the nav and wordmark fall back to the browser default font — not even serif. While `font-headline` has `"serif"` fallback. This makes the header more fragile than the rest. Also inconsistent: header uses arbitrary values, pages use tokens — two systems for the same type roles.

3. **Layout.astro footer/header use `font-['Newsreader']`** (no fallback) and the support nav button uses `font-['Newsreader']` while the same CTA treatment on pages uses `font-label`. Confirmed inconsistency.

4. Now the hotspot bug — let me re-verify the overflow claim by checking the built CSS ordering. Actually, the key claim: `.hotspot-image { overflow: visible; }` in global.css overrides the `overflow-hidden` utility on the figure (className="rounded-2xl shadow-xl overflow-hidden"). In Tailwind v4, utilities live in `@layer utilities`. Unlayered rules (`.hotspot-image` in global.css is written at top level, unlayered) win over ALL layered rules. So yes — overflow: visible wins, rounded corners NOT clipped for the image, dots bleed. Confirmed at the CSS level.

   Wait — I should double-check where global.css is imported and whether its rules are inside `@layer base` or unlayered. Looking at global.css: `@layer base { ... }` contains only focus styles and skip-link and btn-touch. Everything else (`.hotspot-image`, `.reveal`, etc.) is written unlayered. The `@theme` block is special (Tailwind). So unlayered custom CSS overrides layered utilities. Confirmed.

   Actually, one more nuance: does `border-radius: inherit` on `.hotspot-image` even work? `.hotspot-image` is the `figure` element with `rounded-2xl` utility — border-radius: 0.75rem from the utility. `.hotspot-image { border-radius: inherit }` — inherit from parent... The figure's own border-radius comes from its own class; `border-radius: inherit` would inherit from the parent element (main section), overriding the utility! Since `.hotspot-image` is unlayered and `.rounded-2xl` is layered, `.hotspot-image`'s `border-radius: inherit` wins → figure inherits border-radius from parent (which has none) → radius = 0! So the figure on ourlady has NO border radius at all (inherits none), NO clipping (overflow visible), and the image is square-cornered. The intended rounded-2xl photo frame on the ourlady main image is completely broken at the CSS level. Both properties (`border-radius: inherit` and `overflow: visible`) override the utilities. Double-confirmed bug: "rounded-2xl photo frames" don't apply to the hotspot figure.

5. The dark-theme hotspot card contrast bug — verified via tokens: `--color-on-surface` is overridden per dark theme to a light color, `--color-inverse-on-surface` is never overridden (stays #f2f1ec light). So `.hotspot-card { background: var(--color-on-surface); color: var(--color-inverse-on-surface); }` = light-on-light on all dark themes. Confirmed.

   Wait — actually let me double-check that `.hotspot-card` color token. `background: var(--color-on-surface)` — natt: #e8f4ff (very light). `color: var(--color-inverse-on-surface)` — default #f2f1ec (light). Yes, light-on-light. And `.hotspot-card strong` inherits. `.hotspot-label` background hardcoded rgba(251,249,244,0.92) light with `color: var(--color-on-surface)` light on dark themes — light-on-light. Confirmed.

6. The footer copyright `text-on-surface-variant/60` at text-xs — contrast issue. #43474e at 60% over #fbf9f4 ≈ blend: 0.6*67 + 0.4*251 ≈ 40+100 = 140-ish? Let me compute roughly: 0.6×0x43(67)+0.4×0xfb(251) = 40.2+100.4 = 140.6; 0.6×0x47(71)+0.4×0xf9(249)=42.6+99.6=142.2; 0.6×0x4e(78)+0.4×0xf4(244)=46.8+97.6=144.4 → ~#8d8e90. Contrast vs #fbf9f4: relative luminance of #8d8e90 ≈ 0.28; #fbf9f4 ≈ 0.94. Ratio = (0.94+0.05)/(0.28+0.05) = 0.99/0.33 ≈ 3.0:1 — fails 4.5:1 for 12px text. Confirmed as a genuine low-contrast issue. Also on dark themes, `text-on-surface-variant` is a light color (natt #b8d8f0) at 60% over near-black — blend ~40% luminance... roughly 0.6*0.63+0.4*0.02 ≈ 0.38 → contrast ~ (0.38+0.05)/(0.02+0.05) ≈ 6:1? Hmm, #b8d8f0 luminance ≈ 0.63. 60% over #050a12 (0.01) → ~0.38. Ratio ≈ 0.43/0.06 ≈ 7:1. OK on dark themes it's fine; on the light default it fails. 

7. Mobile nav — confirmed `hidden sm:inline-flex` on all three nav links with no mobile menu anywhere; footer has no page links either. The plans page is unreachable on mobile. Confirmed.

8. Language switcher always links home pages. Confirmed by reading Layout.

9. Logo link → `/capellareginaenorvegiae` root → meta-refresh to /no. Confirmed (pages/index.astro).

10. H1 size inversion: home hero md:text-6xl (60px), story/plans md:text-7xl (72px). Confirmed.

11. The support page: no `.reveal` usage; motion inconsistency. Confirmed.

12. The support two-column donor grid with conditional second column. Confirmed potential lopsided layout if recentDonors empty. Actually if `recentDonors.length === 0` the whole inner div is not rendered, so grid has one child → occupies col 1 of 2 on md. Lopsided. But data-dependent — if always populated, fine. Note it.

13. Lightbox: no focus trap/focus return; zoom-in affordance hover-only. Confirmed.

14. BeforeAfterSlider: hardcoded #36557b handle arrows (theme-invariant). Confirmed. Also the slider is keyboard-operable — good. The labels "before"/"after" — the before label top-right, after label top-left inside clip — good.

15. No `initial-scale=1` in viewport meta. Confirmed line 11 of Layout.

16. Page `<title>` identical on all pages. Confirmed.

17. The giant THESIS comment in Layout (lines 27–38) ships into every HTML page. Confirmed.

18. DESIGN.md referenced in the comment but doesn't exist. Confirmed by find.

19. Support page H1 and ourlady H1 use text-5xl md:text-6xl while story/plans use text-5xl md:text-7xl — 3 size tiers. Confirmed.

20. The `.reveal` on story/plans header has no no-JS fallback (content opacity 0 until JS runs; if IO unsupported, permanently invisible). Actually the reveal elements: story header section and plans header section only. Home has no reveal. OK.

21. The hero section on home: `aria-label={idx.galleryLabel}` — "The chapel" — screenreader name for a section containing the h1. Minor.

22. The hero image: `<Image ... class="absolute inset-0 w-full h-full object-cover" />` — no alt width/height constraints issue. Fine.

23. **The theme panel lacks a visible label** — the floating palette button has aria-label="Change theme" — good.

24. **The theme panel hardcodes colors** for swatches — fine. But it's `bg-black/40 backdrop-blur-xl` translucent — when the theme panel is open over the hero photo, the black/40 panel with text colored per button — readable. OK.

25. **Default theme & saved theme interplay**: If user picks a dark theme, reloads — inline script sets data-theme before CSS loads? The inline script is in `<head>`; CSS is linked earlier (global.css is imported by Layout via `import "../styles/global.css"` — Astro bundles that into a `<link>` in head). The head script runs after CSS parse — order: the stylesheet link appears before the script (imports are hoisted to head before other head content? Astro places imported CSS link in head). Either way, once the script runs, theme set. There may be a brief flash of light theme before the script runs if the CSS loads before the script executes — but the script is inline in head right after the font links, before body. Since the script is synchronous and before body, no FOUC. Good.

26. Also the theme switcher — **no `color-scheme` update** — scrollbars/inputs remain light. Minor.

27. `main id="main-content"` missing on 4 pages → skip link broken. Confirmed.

28. Let me also double check `story` page drop cap: `.prose-custom > p:first-of-type::first-letter` — the first section (The building) — the drop cap floats; the second paragraph starts right after. OK. On the NO page, the first paragraph starts with "Smia på Ledum gård" — drop cap "S" — fine.

29. `heading` on ourlady blocks: h2 `text-3xl italic text-center` — 30px Newsreader italic centered — fine.

30. One more potential design break: **the home page photo grid**: `sidealter` full-width h-[44vh] md:h-[68vh] object-cover; below it two 2:3 portraits. On mobile, `h-[44vh]` side altar photo then two portrait photos stacked → the rhythm is: 44vh landscape, then two tall portraits. OK. But the "What it is" section has no heading, no text — just photos and two links. Feels unfinished, and the dead `whatHeading` confirms the intent to label it.

31. **Video on home**: The YouTube thumbnail/first frame is a dark video player — `aspect-video rounded-2xl shadow-xl` — fine. 

32. **The hero CTA contrast**: `bg-white text-primary` — on the Fjord default #36557b on white = 8:1 fine.

33. **Header nav links** at text-base Newsreader italic — the active page gets `underline decoration-secondary decoration-2` — amber underline under italic blue serif — the amber underline at underline-offset-4. It's OK. But there is no active styling for the support pill beyond bg change; the pill uses `bg-surface-container` when active — subtle.

34. **The `hidden sm:block` subtitle "Gudbrandsdalen"** — hidden on mobile; on desktop, small label under wordmark — good.

35. **The footer**: `mt-20` on footer — with pb-24 on some mains, spacing OK. The footer divider star `text-secondary text-sm ✦` at opacity-40 — fine.

36. **`.btn-touch` class** defined in base but never used (buttons use min-h-[44px] directly). Dead CSS. Minor.

37. **The `font-label` used in theme panel buttons but the panel itself is Epilogue** — the buttons are 14px Epilogue — fine.

38. Also check: `--font-headline: "Newsreader", "serif"` — with italic applied as utility `italic` — fine.

39. **The theme switcher overlaps the lightbox?** Lightbox z-[100] vs theme switcher z-50 — lightbox covers switcher. Fine.

40. **Hotspot on ourlady has only ONE hotspot** ("Kronen" / the crown at 49%, 18%) — one dot on a big image. Sparse, but content-limited. The single hotspot positioned near the top center — the crown — OK.

Also: the ourlady main image with the hotspot — `varfrue.jpg` — I can't view it. The hotspot at y=18% — on the crown of Mary. Fine.

41. The `hotspot-label` is always rendered in DOM (opacity 0) — with `white-space: nowrap` — "Kronen" is short. OK.

42. **Missing `figure` caption styling on plans** — no captions at all under sketches; fine.

43. **The plans page `imageGroups` uses `block.images === "scale"`** — the grid columns `grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3` for scale (5 images → 3+2 ragged final row) and `grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2` for work (2) and apsis (2). 5 images in 3-col grid = 3+2 — ragged last row. With varying aspect ratios, the tiles will be uneven heights. Minor.

44. **The theme switcher is a single global FAB** — 8 themes including Natt, Aurora, etc. The whole "8-theme switcher" is a design-system gimmick: for a chapel site with warm photography, five of the eight themes (Natt, Kull, Solnedgang, Aurora, Is) are electric/dark modes that fight the warm art direction; and since 5 themes are dark, the photo-driven pages keep warm daylight photos on dark electric backgrounds — a jarring mismatch. The theme system adds maintenance cost (they've already missed pulse-ring variants for is/mose, hotspot card contrast, etc.). Blunt critique: the theme system is the biggest design liability — it produces inconsistencies that ship (hotspot tooltip invisible on 5/8 themes).

45. Also **`data-theme` on `document.documentElement`** — the CSS selectors `[data-theme="natt"]` etc. — good. The `@theme` default applies when no data-theme. The `fundraiser-panel` default is parchment. In "is" theme (light blue), panel is blue-tinted; fine.

46. **Dead `old/` and `Welcome.astro`** — the old/ folder contains index.html and assets — legacy. Not shipped presumably (it's a folder in repo root, not under public). Fine — but it means the repo carries a dead legacy copy. Not a shipped design issue.

47. **Missing DESIGN.md** — the Layout comment claims the build "ends with the finish review, the verdict, and DESIGN.md" — none exist. Also `.impeccable/surfaces/` files — evidence of process. The surface file for index — fine.

48. One more real thing: **the `hidden` + `flex` class dance for the theme panel** — `class="hidden flex-col gap-1 ..."` — JS toggles `hidden` and adds `flex`. Good. Initial `aria-expanded="false"` — toggled. Good.

49. **The theme panel buttons have no `type="button"`** — but they're not in a form. Fine.

50. **The support nav button `rounded-sm`** vs theme button `rounded-xl` — minor.

51. **`leading-tight` on the wordmark div** — fine.

52. Also: **`text-on-surface-variant` on the home visit panel body** — #43474e on #f5f3ee — ~7.5:1 fine.

53. **`text-primary/80` inline links on home** (storyLink, ourLadyLink) — #36557b at 80% on #fbf9f4 → blend ≈ #6a7f9d? Luminance ~0.2 → contrast ~4.8:1 — borderline for large italic text (text-lg). Fine-ish for 18px text (needs 4.5 only below 24px/18.66px bold; 18px non-bold needs 4.5). ~4.8 passes narrowly. On "is" theme primary #001040 → fine. On dark themes primary bright → fine.

54. **The `bg-white/90` hover on the white hero button** — fine.

55. **The hero button + Instagram link on the same line** — the map CTA (Epilogue, uppercase? no, not uppercase — `tracking-wide`) vs italic serif text link. Fine but the two links carry unequal visual weight for what the thesis says is the primary action. The Instagram link is actually more prominent typographically (text-lg italic serif) than the button content (text-sm Epilogue). The primary action (map) is presented smaller than the secondary (Instagram). An inversion of the stated intent.

OK. I think I have a comprehensive picture. Also let me quickly check the build folder to see if DESIGN.md lives there or whether there are other design docs. Already checked — no DESIGN.md. 

Let me also verify the "is" and "mose" missing pulse keyframes claim — confirmed in the CSS: keyframes exist for natt, kull, skog, solnedgang, aurora only. But `.btn-pulse` is never used in any page — dead code anyway. So it's a latent issue, not an active one. I'll note it as dead-code + latent.

Let me also double check whether the nav links might be reachable on mobile via the support page back links or elsewhere — the only nav structure is the header. Confirmed no mobile menu.

Also the header uses `hidden sm:inline-flex` — at the `sm` breakpoint (640px) the nav appears — so mobile (<640px) loses story/ourlady/plans. And the language switcher is always visible — taking space. So on mobile, header = logo + NO|EN + Support pill. Story/ourlady/plans unreachable. Confirmed.

One more check — the footer only has Instagram + language links. Confirmed no page links in footer.

Now, is the plans page reachable from any page other than the nav? Home doesn't link plans. Story doesn't. Ourlady doesn't. Support doesn't. So on desktop, the ONLY path to Plans is the header nav; on mobile there's no path at all. Confirmed critical navigation hole.

Let me also confirm the title duplication and check dist build to see what ships. Not necessary.

Also, let me confirm `before`/`after` images in the slider: `before.jpeg`, `afterv2-1.jpg` — afterv2 — second version. OK.

Also the slider hint uses `font-sketch text-tertiary` — Caveat handwriting for a functional hint — small (text-base) caveat at tertiary color. On default theme tertiary #5d5142 (brownish gray) — on surface #fbf9f4 — contrast ~7:1 OK.

One more possible design break — **the ourlady layout on mobile**: main image (hotspot) full width, then close-up portrait below — fine.

**The ourlady page heading**: `text-5xl md:text-6xl italic` — "Vår Frue av Gudbrandsdalen" — at 60px italic Newsreader — long word "Gudbrandsdalen" — may wrap awkwardly at max-w-6xl centered — fine.

Also, **`leading-tight` vs `leading-snug` vs `leading-relaxed`** mix — fine.

**The drop cap color `var(--color-primary)`** — on dark themes bright — fine.

Now, one thing I should double-check: is `--color-primary: #36557b` and `--color-secondary: #7b581e` used consistently? Yes, both defined in @theme. Also `--color-tertiary: #5d5142`. The three-hue system (blue primary, amber secondary, brown-gray tertiary) — a coherent M3-based palette. The dark themes each pick their own hues — so the "Fjord system" identity (slate blue + amber) is discarded in 7/8 themes. The theme system thus multiplies brand identity — each theme is a different brand. For a chapel site with warm photography, this is the core art-direction critique.

Also, the **hero title color `text-white` and intro `text-white/90`** over photo — good.

**The bottom picture full-bleed**: `h-[60vh] md:h-[72vh] object-cover` — full-bleed square-cornered image directly above the footer — the footer has border-t border-outline-variant — a hard line between the photo and footer. The photo is a closing statement but has no caption/overlay — and the dead closeImgAlt/closeInstagram keys show a planned closing treatment was dropped, leaving a bare full-bleed image. Unfinished.

Also **the reel section is between visit panel and bottom picture** — order: photos → links → visit panel → video → bottom photo. The video sits oddly between the visit CTA and the closing image; the thesis says "story and support recede to quiet links" — but the video is a big media block with a heading. Fine.

Let me also verify **`content` `idx.support` key** — "Support us" — dead (the nav uses `t("nav.support")` from ui.ts). Dead key.

Now compile the review. Structure:

Priority list (worst first):
1. **CRITICAL — Mobile navigation collapse** (Layout.astro:77-99): nav links hidden below sm; no menu replacement; footer has no page links; plans unreachable on mobile entirely; plans only reachable via header on desktop.
2. **HIGH — Hotspot figure frame is broken at the CSS level** (global.css:488-490 `.hotspot-image { border-radius: inherit; overflow: visible; }`): unlayered rules beat Tailwind's layered `rounded-2xl overflow-hidden` utilities; on the ourlady page the figure loses both its radius and its clipping — square corners, pulse rings bleed. Fix: remove those two declarations, put radius on the img or keep overflow-hidden.
3. **HIGH — Hotspot tooltip/label invisible on all 5 dark themes** (global.css:507-516, 528-533): card bg = var(--color-on-surface) which is light in dark themes; color = var(--color-inverse-on-surface) never overridden → stays light #f2f1ec → light-on-light. Hotspot label bg hardcoded rgba(251,249,244,0.92) with color on-surface — same. Fix: use tokens that invert: bg var(--color-inverse-surface), color var(--color-on-surface), or define per-theme overrides.
4. **HIGH — Broken skip link on 4 of 5 pages** (Layout.astro:57 → only index.astro:29 has id="main-content").
5. **MEDIUM-HIGH — Header/logo language bug** (Layout.astro:63): logo href points to base root which meta-refreshes to /no; clicking the logo from an English page dumps you to Norwegian home. Language switcher (Layout.astro:104-111) always links to home, discarding current page context.
6. **MEDIUM — Inverted H1 scale** (index.astro:40 md:text-6xl vs story.astro:30/plans.astro:52 md:text-7xl): interior headers bigger than the flagship photo-hero headline; three different H1 sizes across four pages (6xl home/ourlady/support, 7xl story/plans).
7. **MEDIUM — Home page section 2 is an unlabeled photo dump** (index.astro:66-105): no heading, no caption; dead `whatHeading` key; the planned Instagram close block is gone (dead closeImgAlt/closeInstagram/closeInstagramLabel keys) leaving a bare full-bleed bottom image with no end-card; `idx.support` dead.
8. **MEDIUM — The 8-theme switcher fights the art direction and is the bug factory**: five dark themes recolor the entire brand per-theme (each theme = a different brand); they've already shipped breakages (dark-theme hotspot, missing pulse keyframes for is/mose). Photos stay warm daylight in electric dark chrome. Suggest reducing to 2-3 themes or scoping the switcher, and completing the per-theme overrides.
9. **MEDIUM — Typography system split in two** (Layout.astro:67-116 uses arbitrary `font-['Newsreader']`/`font-['Plus_Jakarta_Sans']`/`font-['Epilogue']` without fallbacks while pages use `font-headline`/`font-label` tokens): if the webfont fails, header/footer/nav fall to a default font, no serif/sans fallback; also the support nav pill is Newsreader italic while the identical CTA role on pages is Epilogue label.
10. **MEDIUM — Hero CTA hierarchy inverted** (index.astro:46-65): primary map CTA is a small Epilogue button; the Instagram link beside it is bigger Newsreader italic — secondary link out-punches the primary action; thesis intent ("How to get here" as THE action) not carried visually.
11. **MEDIUM — Footer copyright contrast fails** (Layout.astro:313 `text-on-surface-variant/60` text-xs ≈ 3.0:1 on default surface) — barely legible small text.
12. **LOW-MED — Lightbox polish** (plans.astro:154-190): no focus management (no focus trap, focus not returned on close, close button not focused); zoom affordance hover-only (touch users get no hint); captions duplicate alt text.
13. **LOW-MED — Before/after slider theme-blind** (BeforeAfterSlider.astro:56 hardcoded #36557b arrows) — on Kull/Solnedgang/Aurora the arrows clash with the theme's palette; also the whole slider is JS-dependent (no-JS = static 50/50, no role).
14. **LOW — Dead code & unfinished artifacts**: Welcome.astro empty; .btn-pulse + 5 pulse keyframes, .timeline-line, .reveal-delay-*, .progress-bar-fill CSS unused (Layout script still queries .progress-bar-fill); btn-touch unused; the giant THESIS comment in Layout ships into every page's HTML; DESIGN.md promised in that comment doesn't exist.
15. **LOW — The .reveal pattern has no no-JS fallback** (global.css:333-336): story/plans headers start at opacity:0; without JS/IntersectionObserver the page header stays invisible. prefers-reduced-motion handles the animation but not the absence of JS.
16. **LOW — Missing initial-scale=1 in viewport meta** (Layout.astro:11); page titles identical across pages; no color-scheme sync with themes.

# Adversarial Design Review — Capella Reginae Norvegiae Read everything: `Layout.astro`, `global.css`, all five pages, both components, i18n content, product doc, dead files. No images could be viewed (no image support in this session), so photography judgment below is confined to what the containers and crop logic do to images, not the pixels themselves. Everything else is verified from source. --- ## BLOCKERS (must fix) ### 1. Mobile navigation collapses; the Plans page is unreachable on mobile **Layout.astro:77, 86, 95** — all three primary links carry `hidden sm:inline-flex`. There is no hamburger, no mobile menu, no fallback nav. The footer (Layout.astro:299–311) only contains Instagram and the two language links. Below 640px, Story / Our Lady / Plans have **zero** navigation paths. And on desktop, Plans is reachable *only* through this header — no page links to Plans anywhere (home links only Story and Our Lady, index.astro:90–102). This is not a minor cosmetic gap: it is the primary navigation of the site disappearing on the exact devices pilgrims will use at the roadside. Fix: add a proper mobile menu (off-canvas or a compact row), and/or add the four page links to the footer. Don't ship this. ### 2. The hotspot photo frame is broken at the CSS level — the Our Lady image has square corners **global.css:576** — `.hotspot-image { border-radius: inherit; overflow: visible; }` is unlayered author CSS. Tailwind v4 puts utilities in `@layer utilities`; **unlayered rules beat layered rules regardless of order**. So on the figure in ourlady.astro:59 (`rounded-2xl shadow-xl overflow-hidden`), both utilities lose: - `border-radius: inherit` replaces the `rounded-2xl` radius (the figure inherits `0` from `
`), and - `overflow: visible` cancels the clipping, so the square-cornered `` pokes out of the intended frame. The comment on the same line claims the opposite of what it does ("Keep hotspot dots from overflowing the rounded image corners" — this code *guarantees* overflow). The pulse ring (global.css:465, `inset: -7px` scaled 1.7×) and tooltips bleed past the photo edge. Fix: delete line 576 entirely, put the radius on the `` itself or rely on `overflow-hidden` on the figure. Then actually verify the rounded frame renders. ### 3. Hotspot tooltip and label are invisible on 5 of the 8 themes **global.css:522–523** — `.hotspot-card { background: var(--color-on-surface); color: var(--color-inverse-on-surface); }`. Every dark theme (natt/kull/solnedgang/aurora, and partially is) overrides `--color-on-surface` to a near-white value (e.g. natt `#e8f4ff`) but **none of them override `--color-inverse-on-surface`**, which stays `#f2f1ec` (light). Result: light text on a light card — the tooltip is unreadable in dark themes. Same disease in the label chip at **global.css:500**: hardcoded warm-white `rgba(251,249,244,.92)` background with `color: var(--color-on-surface)` → light-on-light in every dark theme. Robust fix: flip to `background: var(--color-inverse-surface); color: var(--color-inverse-on-surface)` — both tokens are theme-invariant in this stylesheet (`#30312e`/`#f2f1ec`), so the card becomes dark-with-light-text on *all* themes. This is exactly the class of bug the 8-theme system manufactures. ### 4. Skip link is dead on 4 of 5 pages **Layout.astro:57** — the skip link targets `#main-content`, which exists **only** on the home page (index.astro:29). story.astro, plans.astro, ourlady.astro and support.astro all render `
` without that id. Keyboard users activating "Hopp til innhold" on any interior page get nothing. Fix: add `id="main-content"` to the four `
` elements. --- ## HIGH ### 5. Logo and language switcher destroy language context - **Layout.astro:64** — the wordmark links to `/capellareginaenorvegiae` (no language). pages/index.astro meta-refreshes that to `/no/`. Click the logo from the English page and you land on the *Norwegian* home page. It should be `/${lang}`. - **Layout.astro:103, 108** — the NO/EN links always point at the language root. Switching from `/en/story` takes you to `/no/` (home), not `/no/story`. On a two-language site this is a daily-user footgun, and it makes the per-page underline/nav state feel like a mockup. Fix: translate the current pathname across languages. ### 6. The 8-theme switcher is a brand multiplier and a QA sink — it is already leaking Each theme redefines the entire primary/secondary/tertiary identity (global.css:88–260). The site's actual art direction — slate blue + amber on parchment, warm daylight chapel photography — survives in exactly 1 of 8 themes. Natt's electric cyan, Aurora's magenta-on-teal, Solnedgang's neon orange fight the warm photographs (the photos are the argument; the chrome argues back). The maintenance cost is real and has already shipped breakage: Finding #3 above, plus the pulse animation only has variants for 5 of 7 custom themes (global.css:391–395; is and mose silently reuse the Fjord blue pulse — `.btn-pulse` isn't currently used in any page, so it's a latent trap). Blunt take: either cut the set to 2–3 themes you actually QA in both languages, or accept that every theme adds a full pass of contrast/photo/tooltip work. The current middle state — 8 themes, 2 of them un-verified, 1 broken component — reads as unfinished. ### 7. Inverted display hierarchy: interior pages out-shout the home hero Home hero H1 (index.astro:40) is `md:text-6xl`. Story (story.astro:30) and Plans (plans.astro:52) headers are `md:text-7xl`. The two interior pages have **larger** headlines than the flagship full-bleed hero. And across the four pages you have three different H1 scales (6xl home/ourlady/support, 7xl story/plans). The page you want to be the loudest is the quietest. Fix: unify — hero should be the max, interior headers one step down. ### 8. Home's second section is an unlabeled photo dump; the closing treatment was cut mid-stream The gallery section (index.astro:66–105) has no heading, no caption, no context — two photos, then two serif links floating in space. The heading it was supposed to have exists in content and is dead: `whatHeading: "A quiet room, for everyone."` (content.ts:11). Likewise the planned Instagram end-card is gone but its copy survives dead (content.ts:27–29 `closeImgAlt/closeInstagram/closeInstagramLabel`), leaving a bare full-bleed bottom image (index.astro:150–157) with square corners and no caption — the one image that breaks the rounded-2xl photo system for no visible reason. Either restore the end-card or delete the keys; a bare bleed photo as the last statement looks like an abandoned draft. --- ## MEDIUM ### 9. Typography runs on two parallel systems; the header one is fragile Pages use tokens (`font-headline`/`font-label`/`font-sketch` with fallbacks). The header, nav, and footer use arbitrary values: `font-['Newsreader']` (Layout.astro:67, 77, 86, 95, 116, 289), `font-['Plus_Jakarta_Sans']` (70, 300, 307), `font-['Epilogue']` (102). Arbitrary values compile to `font-family: Newsreader` — **no serif/sans fallback**. If Google Fonts is slow or blocked, the entire chrome renders in the browser default while the pages keep their intended faces. Fix: use `font-headline`/`font-body`/`font-label` in the layout too. Worse: the Support pill (Layout.astro:116) is Newsreader italic, but the identical CTA role on every page (plans.astro:142, story.astro:102, index.astro:51) is an Epilogue label. Same role, two typefaces, in the same viewport. Pick one for the button role. ### 10. Hero CTA hierarchy is inverted index.astro:46–65: the primary action "How to get here" is a `text-sm` Epilogue button; next to it, the secondary Instagram link is `text-lg` Newsreader italic with an underline. The *secondary* link is typographically louder than the *primary* CTA — contradicting the thesis comment in the layout ("the primary action 'How to get here'"). The button should dominate; the Instagram link should read as a quiet footnote. ### 11. Footer copyright fails contrast Layout.astro:313 — `text-xs` + `text-on-surface-variant/60` ≈ `#8d8e90` on `#fbf9f4` ≈ **3.0:1**. Below 4.5:1 for 12px text on the default theme. Either drop the `/60` or bump the size. ### 12. Lightbox is bare-bones interactive furniture plans.astro:157–190: no focus trap (keyboard focus can walk behind the dialog), focus is not moved into the dialog on open nor returned to the trigger on close, the close button is unreachable by keyboard until tabbed to it. The zoom affordance (`zoom_in` badge, plans.astro:128–130) is `group-hover` only — on touch there is zero hint that sketches open. Captions (plans.astro:190) just repeat the alt text, which is contentless ("Scale drawing of the chapel"). For a page whose sole purpose is looking at drawings, the viewer is the page — it deserves focus management and a visible affordance. ### 13. Before/after slider is theme-blind and JS-dependent BeforeAfterSlider.astro:65–66 — the handle arrows are hardcoded `#36557b`. On Kull (copper) and Solnedgang (orange) themes the blue arrows visibly clash. The slider's `role="slider"`, `tabindex`, `aria-valuenow` are all attached from JS (BeforeAfterSlider.astro:68–74) — no JS means a static 50/50 crop with no semantics at all. Fine as a progressive enhancement, but the component should render the semantics server-side. ### 14. Dead code and unfinished artifacts ship in every page - Layout.astro:28–38: a 700-word authorial THESIS essay in an HTML comment — shipped to every visitor, inflating every page. - Dead CSS: `.btn-pulse` + 5 keyframes (global.css:380–395), `.timeline-line` (410), `.progress-bar-fill` (423–427 — Layout.astro:258–265 still queries it), `.reveal-delay-*` (341–343), `.btn-touch` (24). - `Welcome.astro` is an empty shell. - The comment (Layout.astro:55) promises "the finish review, the verdict, and DESIGN.md" — no DESIGN.md exists in the repo. ### 15. Scroll-reveal has no no-JS fallback global.css:332–336 — `.reveal` starts `opacity: 0`; story and plans page headers are `.reveal` (story.astro:24, plans.astro:26). With JS disabled or IntersectionObserver unavailable, the entire page header never appears. `prefers-reduced-motion` (global.css:402) fixes the animation, not the missing JS. Gate the `opacity: 0` behind a `.js` class on ``. --- ## LOW (worth noting) - **Viewport meta** (Layout.astro:24) lacks `initial-scale=1`; **``** (Layout.astro:15) is identical on all five pages; no `theme-color`; themes don't sync `color-scheme` so scrollbars/inputs stay light in dark themes. - **Support donor grid** (support.astro:63–85): `md:grid-cols-2` with a conditionally rendered second column — if "Recent activity" is empty the grid renders one lopsided column with an empty right half. - **Plans sketch grid** (plans.astro:113–119): the "scale" group puts 5 images in `grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3` → ragged 3+2 final row, tiles at natural aspect → uneven row heights. Give the tiles a uniform aspect and `object-contain` on a neutral panel. - **Hotspot hit target** is 36px (global.css:437) vs. the 44px floor used everywhere else. - **Hero section label** `aria-label="The chapel"` (index.astro:32) duplicates the H1 context — harmless but noisy. - The **"What it is" photo crops** are aggressive: `h-[44vh] md:h-[68vh]` object-cover on the side altar, 2:3 forced frames on closeup/chapelside, `h-[60vh]` bottom bleed — worth a human crop-check since object-cover will silently cut faces/candles. - **Fundraiser amount** set in Caveat (support.astro:43) at 60px bold — the handwriting face works as an accent (slider hint, donor amounts) but anchoring the single most important number on the support page in a casual script undercuts "money must stay honest." --- ## What is genuinely right (with evidence) - The token system is coherent where it's complete: M3-style surface hierarchy, primary/secondary/tertiary, per-theme `fundraiser-panel` overrides (global.css:160–260) — the most finished themed component on the site. - Focus-visible styling (global.css:17–22), consistent 44px touch targets, skip link, and reduced-motion handling across reveal/pulse/slider/hotspot (global.css:400–405, 579) — the a11y *foundations* are above average. - The before/after slider is genuinely keyboard-operable with live `aria-valuenow` (BeforeAfterSlider.astro:68–74) — better than most. - The editorial stagger on story (story.astro:78, `md:mt-16`) and the 7/5 column split on ourlady (ourlady.astro:64–77) is well-considered art direction. - Newsreader italic as the display voice is consistent across hero and every interior header — when the sizes are unified, that voice will hold. - The single-hotspot interaction (tap-to-toggle with close-others) is simple and correct in behavior. --- ## Residual risks 1. **Images not visually verified.** I could not render the photos in this session. A click-through in both languages across all 8 themes is required before calling this finished — especially finding #2 and #3, which are invisible in static inspection of a single theme. 3. **Theme count vs. QA budget.** The review found one component already broken in dark themes; there will be more. # Adversarial Design Review — Capella Reginae Norvegiae Read everything: `Layout.astro`, `global.css`, all five pages, both components, i18n content, product doc, dead files. No images could be viewed (no image support in this session), so photography judgment below is confined to what the containers and crop logic do to images, not the pixels themselves. Everything else is verified from source. --- ## BLOCKERS (must fix) ### 1. Mobile navigation collapses; the Plans page is unreachable on mobile **Layout.astro:77, 86, 95** — all three primary links carry `hidden sm:inline-flex`. There is no hamburger, no mobile menu, no fallback nav. The footer (Layout.astro:299–311) only contains Instagram and the two language links. Below 640px, Story / Our Lady / Plans have **zero** navigation paths. And on desktop, Plans is reachable *only* through this header — no page links to Plans anywhere (home links only Story and Our Lady, index.astro:90–102). This is not a minor cosmetic gap: it is the primary navigation of the site disappearing on the exact devices pilgrims will use at the roadside. Fix: add a proper mobile menu (off-canvas or a compact row), and/or add the four page links to the footer. Don't ship this. ### 2. The hotspot photo frame is broken at the CSS level — the Our Lady image has square corners **global.css:576** — `.hotspot-image { border-radius: inherit; overflow: visible; }` is unlayered author CSS. Tailwind v4 puts utilities in `@layer utilities`; **unlayered rules beat layered rules regardless of order**. So on the figure in ourlady.astro:59 (`rounded-2xl shadow-xl overflow-hidden`), both utilities lose: - `border-radius: inherit` replaces the `rounded-2xl` radius (the figure inherits `0` from `
`), and - `overflow: visible` cancels the clipping, so the square-cornered `` pokes out of the intended frame. The comment on the same line claims the opposite of what it does ("Keep hotspot dots from overflowing the rounded image corners" — this code *guarantees* overflow). The pulse ring (global.css:465, `inset: -7px` scaled 1.7×) and tooltips bleed past the photo edge. Fix: delete line 576 entirely, put the radius on the `` itself or rely on `overflow-hidden` on the figure. Then actually verify the rounded frame renders. ### 3. Hotspot tooltip and label are invisible on 5 of the 8 themes **global.css:522–523** — `.hotspot-card { background: var(--color-on-surface); color: var(--color-inverse-on-surface); }`. Every dark theme (natt/kull/solnedgang/aurora, and partially is) overrides `--color-on-surface` to a near-white value (e.g. natt `#e8f4ff`) but **none of them override `--color-inverse-on-surface`**, which stays `#f2f1ec` (light). Result: light text on a light card — the tooltip is unreadable in dark themes. Same disease in the label chip at **global.css:500**: hardcoded warm-white `rgba(251,249,244,.92)` background with `color: var(--color-on-surface)` → light-on-light in every dark theme. Robust fix: flip to `background: var(--color-inverse-surface); color: var(--color-inverse-on-surface)` — both tokens are theme-invariant in this stylesheet (`#30312e`/`#f2f1ec`), so the card becomes dark-with-light-text on *all* themes. This is exactly the class of bug the 8-theme system manufactures. ### 4. Skip link is dead on 4 of 5 pages **Layout.astro:57** — the skip link targets `#main-content`, which exists **only** on the home page (index.astro:29). story.astro, plans.astro, ourlady.astro and support.astro all render `
` without that id. Keyboard users activating "Hopp til innhold" on any interior page get nothing. Fix: add `id="main-content"` to the four `
` elements. --- ## HIGH ### 5. Logo and language switcher destroy language context - **Layout.astro:64** — the wordmark links to `/capellareginaenorvegiae` (no language). pages/index.astro meta-refreshes that to `/no/`. Click the logo from the English page and you land on the *Norwegian* home page. It should be `/${lang}`. - **Layout.astro:103, 108** — the NO/EN links always point at the language root. Switching from `/en/story` takes you to `/no/` (home), not `/no/story`. On a two-language site this is a daily-user footgun, and it makes the per-page underline/nav state feel like a mockup. Fix: translate the current pathname across languages. ### 6. The 8-theme switcher is a brand multiplier and a QA sink — it is already leaking Each theme redefines the entire primary/secondary/tertiary identity (global.css:88–260). The site's actual art direction — slate blue + amber on parchment, warm daylight chapel photography — survives in exactly 1 of 8 themes. Natt's electric cyan, Aurora's magenta-on-teal, Solnedgang's neon orange fight the warm photographs (the photos are the argument; the chrome argues back). The maintenance cost is real and has already shipped breakage: Finding #3 above, plus the pulse animation only has variants for 5 of 7 custom themes (global.css:391–395; is and mose silently reuse the Fjord blue pulse — `.btn-pulse` isn't currently used in any page, so it's a latent trap). Blunt take: either cut the set to 2–3 themes you actually QA in both languages, or accept that every theme adds a full pass of contrast/photo/tooltip work. The current middle state — 8 themes, 2 of them un-verified, 1 broken component — reads as unfinished. ### 7. Inverted display hierarchy: interior pages out-shout the home hero Home hero H1 (index.astro:40) is `md:text-6xl`. Story (story.astro:30) and Plans (plans.astro:52) headers are `md:text-7xl`. The two interior pages have **larger** headlines than the flagship full-bleed hero. And across the four pages you have three different H1 scales (6xl home/ourlady/support, 7xl story/plans). The page you want to be the loudest is the quietest. Fix: unify — hero should be the max, interior headers one step down. ### 8. Home's second section is an unlabeled photo dump; the closing treatment was cut mid-stream The gallery section (index.astro:66–105) has no heading, no caption, no context — two photos, then two serif links floating in space. The heading it was supposed to have exists in content and is dead: `whatHeading: "A quiet room, for everyone."` (content.ts:11). Likewise the planned Instagram end-card is gone but its copy survives dead (content.ts:27–29 `closeImgAlt/closeInstagram/closeInstagramLabel`), leaving a bare full-bleed bottom image (index.astro:150–157) with square corners and no caption — the one image that breaks the rounded-2xl photo system for no visible reason. Either restore the end-card or delete the keys; a bare bleed photo as the last statement looks like an abandoned draft. --- ## MEDIUM ### 9. Typography runs on two parallel systems; the header one is fragile Pages use tokens (`font-headline`/`font-label`/`font-sketch` with fallbacks). The header, nav, and footer use arbitrary values: `font-['Newsreader']` (Layout.astro:67, 77, 86, 95, 116, 289), `font-['Plus_Jakarta_Sans']` (70, 300, 307), `font-['Epilogue']` (102). Arbitrary values compile to `font-family: Newsreader` — **no serif/sans fallback**. Same role, two typefaces, in the same viewport. Pick one for the button role. ### 10. The zoom affordance (`zoom_in` badge, plans.astro:128–130) is `group-hover` only — on touch there is zero hint that sketches open. Captions (plans.astro:190) just repeat the alt text, which is contentless ("Scale drawing of the chapel"). For a page whose sole purpose is looking at drawings, the viewer is the page — it deserves focus management and a visible affordance. ### 13. Before/after slider is theme-blind and JS-dependent BeforeAfterSlider.astro:65–66 — the handle arrows are hardcoded `#36557b`. On Kull (copper) and Solnedgang (orange) themes the blue arrows visibly clash. The slider's `role="slider"`, `tabindex`, `aria-valuenow` are all attached from JS (BeforeAfterSlider.astro:68–74) — no JS means a static 50/50 crop with no semantics at all. Fine as a progressive enhancement, but the component should render the semantics server-side. ### 14. Gate the `opacity: 0` behind a `.js` class on ``. --- ## LOW (worth noting) - **Viewport meta** (Layout.astro:24) lacks `initial-scale=1`; **``** (Layout.astro:15) is identical on all five pages; no `theme-color`; themes don't sync `color-scheme` so scrollbars/inputs stay light in dark themes. - **Support donor grid** (support.astro:63–85): `md:grid-cols-2` with a conditionally rendered second column — if "Recent activity" is empty the grid renders one lopsided column with an empty right half. - **Plans sketch grid** (plans.astro:113–119): the "scale" group puts 5 images in `grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-3` → ragged 3+2 final row, tiles at natural aspect → uneven row heights.
